title: Cyclic Specialization: cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n, r) and k^{gcd(n,r)} Fixed Colorings
description: Specializes the parent's group-agnostic Burnside master formula |Fix(g)| = k^{cyc(g)} to the cyclic rotation action of ZMod n on an n-bead necklace, recovering the classical number-theoretic count. Writing the rotation group multiplicatively as Rot n = Multiplicative (ZMod n) acting on itself by translation (rotation), the rotation by r is rotation r = Multiplicative.ofAdd r. The headline (A) cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n, r) shows the rotation decomposes the n positions into exactly gcd(n,r) cycles, each of length n/gcd(n,r) = addOrderOf r: the ⟨r⟩-orbit quotient is the coset space Rot n ⧸ ⟨r⟩ (Mathlib's equivSubgroupOrbitsQuotientGroup, valid because translation is pretransitive and cancellative), so cyc(rotation r) = ⟨r⟩.index, and Lagrange plus |⟨r⟩| = n/gcd(n,r) (ZMod.addOrderOf_coe) give the gcd. From (A) the parent's card_fixedBy_eq_pow_cyc yields (B) #(colorings fixed by rotation r) = k^{gcd(n,r)}, and reindexing the parent's averaging identity along Multiplicative.toAdd yields (C) the classical cyclic necklace count ∑_{r:ZMod n} k^{gcd(n,r)} = (#necklaces up to rotation)·n.

overview.historicalContext: Counting k-colored necklaces of n beads up to rotation is the textbook first application of Burnside's lemma. Each rotation by r ∈ Z/nZ has cycle structure consisting of gcd(n,r) cycles of equal length n/gcd(n,r), so it fixes exactly k^{gcd(n,r)} colorings, and the number of distinct necklaces is (1/n)·Σ_{r} k^{gcd(n,r)} (equivalently (1/n)·Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d) k^d). The parent gallery entry burnside-counting-oq-03-oq-02 proved the group-agnostic master formula |Fix(g)| = k^{cyc(g)} for an arbitrary finite group, with cyc(g) the number of ⟨g⟩-orbits, and explicitly asked to recover the cyclic value cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n,r) as a corollary. This entry supplies that bridge: it pins the abstract orbit count cyc to the concrete number-theoretic gcd and re-derives the classical necklace formula as a specialization, not a fresh computation.
overview.problemStatement: For the rotation action of the cyclic group ZMod n on its own n positions, with rotation r the shift x ↦ r + x, prove (A) cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n, r) where cyc is the parent's count of ⟨rotation r⟩-orbits; (B) the number of k-colorings fixed by rotation r equals k^{gcd(n,r)}; and (C) Σ_{r ∈ ZMod n} k^{gcd(n,r)} = (#necklaces up to rotation)·n.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Setup.** Write the rotation group multiplicatively as Rot n = Multiplicative (ZMod n), acting on itself by left translation g • x = g * x (rotation); rotation r := Multiplicative.ofAdd r. Both the group and the position set are Rot n, so the parent's cyc, card_fixedBy_eq_pow_cyc, and Burnside averaging apply verbatim. The action is pretransitive (Regular.isPretransitive) and cancellative (IsCancelSMul for a CancelMonoid).

**(A) cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n,r).** Mathlib's equivSubgroupOrbitsQuotientGroup gives orbitRel.Quotient ⟨r⟩ (Rot n) ≃ Rot n ⧸ ⟨r⟩, so cyc(rotation r) = ⟨r⟩.index (Subgroup.index_eq_card). The cyclic subgroup has size |⟨rotation r⟩| = orderOf (ofAdd r) = addOrderOf r = n / gcd(n,r) (Nat.card_zpowers, orderOf_ofAdd_eq_addOrderOf, ZMod.addOrderOf_coe applied after rewriting r = ↑r.val). Lagrange (Subgroup.card_mul_index) then reads (n/d)·index = n with d = gcd(n,r); since d ∣ n and n ≠ 0, n = (n/d)·d, and cancelling the positive factor n/d (Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left) gives index = d = gcd(n,r).

**(B) k^{gcd(n,r)} fixed colorings.** Apply the parent's card_fixedBy_eq_pow_cyc to rotation r and substitute (A).

**(C) Necklace count.** Reindex the sum ∑_{g:Rot n} k^{cyc g} along the equiv Multiplicative.toAdd : Rot n ≃ ZMod n (Fintype.sum_equiv), rewriting each term by (A) to k^{gcd(n,(toAdd g).val)}; the parent's sum_pow_cyc_eq_card_orbits_mul_card equates the original sum with (#necklaces)·|Rot n| = (#necklaces)·n.
keyInsights: **The abstract orbit count IS the gcd.** cyc(rotation r) is a priori a cardinality of an orbit quotient; identifying that quotient with the coset space Rot n ⧸ ⟨r⟩ turns it into an index, and Lagrange + addOrderOf r = n/gcd(n,r) collapses it to the elementary number gcd(n,r) — the cycle count of a rotation.

**Multiplicative framing for free reuse.** Writing the rotation group as Multiplicative (ZMod n) and acting on itself lets the parent's multiplicative Burnside machinery (cyc, card_fixedBy_eq_pow_cyc, the averaging identity) apply with no re-derivation; rotation r = ofAdd r and the toAdd equiv mediate between the multiplicative proof and the additive ZMod n indexing.

**Translation is free and transitive.** equivSubgroupOrbitsQuotientGroup needs exactly pretransitivity and cancellation, both automatic for the regular action of a group on itself, so the orbit ↔ coset identification is off-the-shelf rather than hand-built.

**Lagrange does the arithmetic.** Rather than count orbit representatives directly, (n/d)·index = n with d ∣ n forces index = d by cancellation — the same Lagrange identity that underlies cyclic-subgroup counting, here specialized to ⟨r⟩ ≤ ZMod n.

**Boundary cases confirm the formula against direct combinatorics.** At r = 0, rotation 0 is the identity of Rot n, so gcd(n,0) = n gives cyc(rotation 0) = n: every position is its own singleton orbit, matching the trivial fact that the identity fixes all k^n colorings, and (B) collapses to k^n as expected. At the opposite extreme, when gcd(n,r) = 1 (r generates ZMod n), cyc(rotation r) = 1 — the rotation is a single n-cycle through all positions — so (B) forces only the k monochromatic colorings to survive, k^{gcd(n,r)} = k, the tightest term in the sum (C).

overview.what: The cyclic specialization of Burnside orbit-counting: for the rotation action of ZMod n on an n-bead necklace, the rotation by r has exactly gcd(n,r) cycles, fixes k^{gcd(n,r)} colorings, and the number of distinct necklaces up to rotation is (1/n)·Σ_{r} k^{gcd(n,r)}.
overview.how: Identify the ⟨r⟩-orbit quotient with the coset space Rot n ⧸ ⟨r⟩ (free transitive action) so cyc(rotation r) = ⟨r⟩.index, compute |⟨r⟩| = n/gcd(n,r) via ZMod.addOrderOf_coe, and use Lagrange to read off index = gcd(n,r); then feed this into the parent's k^{cyc(g)} formula and Burnside averaging.
overview.significance: Closes the gap the parent entry explicitly flagged (openQuestions[0]): it derives the concrete cyclic value cyc(rotation r) = gcd(n,r) from the abstract group-agnostic count, so the classical necklace formula k^{gcd(n,r)} and its average (1/n)·Σ_r k^{gcd(n,r)} become specializations of one theorem rather than a separate bespoke computation. This grounds every cyclic necklace count in the gallery in the general Burnside machinery and demonstrates that the abstract cyc invariant computes to the expected elementary number theory.

references.note: Establishes the transitive case of the orbit-counting lemma (average number of fixed points equals the number of orbits) — the earliest source for what is now called the Cauchy–Frobenius–Burnside lemma underlying this necklace count.

references.note: Popularized the orbit-counting lemma — hence the common name 'Burnside's lemma' — though Burnside himself attributed it to Frobenius; the k-colored necklace count is its textbook first application.
